places.name: Deer Pond Farm
places.note: A Connecticut Audubon sanctuary of about 850 acres spanning the Sherman/Pawling line, with roughly 15 miles of trails open dawn to dusk year-round, free of charge. Parking at 57 Wakeman Hill Road. Dogs, bikes and drones are prohibited; a visitor center hosts programs and exhibits.

places.name: Hadlow Preserve
places.note: A 45-acre working hayfield preserve where a mowed perimeter path of about 1 to 1.5 miles climbs past stone walls and sugar maples to a hilltop with westward views — NCLC calls it the best place for kite flying, and a favorite for picnics and fall hawk-watching. Roadside parking near the gate at 9 Cozier Hill Road; stay on the field perimeter (private land lies north of the stone wall) and respect farm equipment.

places.name: Upland Pastures
places.note: NCLC conservation land off Upland Pastures Road (former Osborne family farmland, deeded to Naromi Land Trust). Not on NCLC's formal trail-preserve list, but in regular local use for quiet walking — confirmed first-hand. The adjacent Towner Hill Preserve trailhead connects the area.

sources: Field-verified in person by the site maintainer (Sherman resident), 2026-08-03

places.name: McKinney NWR — Salt Meadow Unit
places.note: Refuge headquarters. Interpretive trail through salt marsh, shrubland and meadow. Open daily, half hour before sunrise to half hour after sunset.

places.name: McKinney NWR — Milford Point Unit
places.note: Barrier beach; one of the best birdwatching spots in Connecticut. Observation deck at the entrance. Piping plover and least tern nesting habitat.

places.name: McKinney NWR — Sheffield Island Unit
places.note: Nature trail, sandy beach and the 1868 Sheffield Island lighthouse. Reached by seasonal Norwalk Seaport Association ferry or private boat.

places.name: McKinney NWR — Calf Island Unit
places.fee: Free (boat launch fee at Byram Park)
places.note: A roughly 30-acre island off Greenwich's Byram shore, part of Stewart B. McKinney National Wildlife Refuge. Open daily from 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes after sunset with beach and trail access — but there is no ferry or dock, so visitors must arrive by private boat (kayaks may land on designated beaches). Obey posted habitat closures.

places.name: Town of Colebrook land
places.note: A 700-acre seasonal flood-control reservoir off Route 8 north of Winsted, open to the public at no charge during daylight hours. Boat launch, trout and bass fishing, and wildlife viewing; foot access is allowed year-round, though areas can close on short notice for flood control.

places.name: West Thompson Lake
places.fee: Free day use; camping fees apply
places.note: Army Corps of Engineers flood-control land along the Quinebaug River with a 200-acre lake, over 9 miles of marked hiking trails, a boat ramp, canoe launch, free disc golf course, picnicking and a seasonal campground. Day use is free.

places.note: A 142-acre NCLC preserve spanning Gaylordsville and Sherman, with a roughly 1.5-mile round-trip trail between trailheads on Gaylord Road and 64 Edmonds Road. places.name: Irene's Woods Preserve
places.note: Trails lead from Hubbell Mountain Road past vernal pools to a flat-rock overlook, a split rock outcrop, and on to Route 37, with Eagle Scout-built steps through a small stream gorge. Roadside pull-off parking at 15 Hubbell Mountain Road; adjoins Towner Hill Preserve.

places.name: Towner Hill Preserve
places.note: An 81-acre preserve known for massive glacial erratics and a boulder field, with easterly views after leaf-fall and lively vernal pools in spring. Trailhead and gravel parking at 46 CT-37 East. Adjoins Irene's Woods for a longer combined hike.

places.name: West Briggs Hill Preserve
places.note: An 84-acre preserve whose single blazed loop starts with a steep climb, then rolls through forest past historic stone walls and old-growth trees; popular with trail runners and birdwatchers. Roadside parking with a kiosk at 23 Briggs Hill Road. Can be muddy in spring.

places.name: Brookland and Josephson Preserves
places.note: About 86 acres of hardwood forest where a green-and-white blazed loop of roughly 2.5 miles crosses the Naromiyocknowhusunkatankshunk Brook on stepping stones and footbridges. Trailhead at 18 Crooked Furrows Lane; parking for about 3 cars.

places.name: Wimisink Preserve
places.note: Two boardwalks — a 330-foot wheelchair-accessible northern one and a 400-foot southern one — extend into a calcium-rich freshwater marsh with active beavers. A viewing platform overlooks habitat famous for American and Least Bitterns; a designated Important Bird Area. Parking on Route 39 North near Route 55.

places.name: Mallory Preserve
places.note: A 120-acre NCLC preserve beside Sherman's town center: a boardwalk through a maple wetland, a rolling loop along Sawmill Brook, and steeper yellow and blue trails up Turner Mountain with seasonal views. Park at the Sherman Town Center lot; the trailhead is near 15 Route 39 North.
